definitions.explanation: A disposable napkin made of paper, commonly provided at restaurants, cafes, and fast-food establishments.

examples.japanese: {紙|かみ}ナプキンを{取|と}ってください。
examples.english: Please pass me a paper napkin.

examples.japanese: テーブルの{上|うえ}に{紙|かみ}ナプキンが{置|お}いてある。
examples.english: There are paper napkins on the table.

examples.japanese: {子|こ}どもが{飲|の}み{物|もの}をこぼしたので、{紙|かみ}ナプキンで{拭|ふ}いた。
examples.english: The child spilled their drink, so I wiped it up with a paper napkin.

notes:
A compound of {紙|かみ} (paper) and ナプキン (napkin, from English). In Japan, restaurants often provide おしぼり (wet towels) instead of paper napkins, so {紙|かみ}ナプキン is more associated with Western-style restaurants and fast-food chains.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {紙|かみ}ナプキンで{拭|ふ}く: to wipe with a paper napkin
- {紙|かみ}ナプキンを{広|ひろ}げる: to unfold a paper napkin
- {紙|かみ}ナプキンホルダー: napkin holder/dispenser

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ナプキン: napkin — the base word; in Japanese, also commonly refers to sanitary napkins
- おしぼり: wet towel — provided at Japanese restaurants for hand-wiping
- ティッシュ: tissue paper — for the nose or general-purpose wiping
